title: Israel Police shut down internal messaging apps as a precaution, Al Ghad reports
date_note: The page gives only its publication day, 24 November.
geo_basis: country-level pin; the article names no city
summary: Al Ghad reports that Israel Police disabled their internal messaging and communication apps over fears sensitive information could leak, disrupting instant contact with officers in the field. Al Ghad says police described a "complex technical incident" and a precautionary shutdown, and that Hebrew media reported police had not determined whether it was a cyberattack or an external technical failure. Al Ghad says it is unclear whether unauthorised parties accessed data.
plain: Israeli police switched off their internal messaging apps as a precaution. Reports say it is not yet known whether it was an attack or a technical fault.
exec: A national police force lost its internal messaging tools; per Al Ghad, the cause is undetermined.

validation.note: Al Ghad and Shorouk News were read; both relay police statements and Hebrew-media reports (Shorouk cites Euronews), so treated as one chain. No police page was read.

review.note: Compared title, date, precaution shutdown, undetermined cause and attribution to Al Ghad against the article; outage-as-attack flag is a relayed statement only
